conservation.condition_narrative: The object is in good and stable condition. The object is a preparatory sketch for the painting Brooklyn Bridge (77.11), also in the museum's collection. Horizontal creases near the upper edge of the sheet may have been created when the sheet was attached to a drawing board or possibly the painting's masonite panel as a means to transfer the friable drawing media to the primed panel. A myriad of creases down the center vertical axis of the sheet may have been created by the artist if she folded the paper in half lengthwise, to transfer the design from one half of hte sheet to the other, for symmetry. Another possible theory is that the creases were created due to repetative folding the sheet to transfer the composition to the primed masonite panel. Horizontal creases throughout the sheet may have been created when the drawing was rolled in storage or may also be related to the artist's process. Two small punctures near each of the upper corners suggest the drawing was pinned to a surface. There are six strips of Japanese paper on the verso from a previous hinging campaign: two along the upper edge of the sheet, near the corners; two along the left edge; and two along the right edge. Abrasions and residual adhesive in two areas just above the center of the verso appear to have been created by tape, now removed.
